title: Beta window first-response playbook and KPI cue sheet
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a compact, operational checklist and KPI tracker for the first 72 hours of a closed beta window. It focuses on: first-response cadence, early signal detection (quality & infra), immediate customer communication, and lightweight gating decisions.

Scope: 
- Applies to product feature launches that are gated as closed betas (invite-only, rolling cohorts).
- Intended audience: product-ops lead, on-call SRE, solutions engineering, and assigned PM/EM.
- Not a replacement for full launch playbooks (use Product-Ops Launch Roadmap for full go-live).

Beta window timeline (example 14-day window with concentrated early ops):
- Day -3: Internal readiness check (observability links, Slack channel, monitoring dashboards shared).
- Day 0: Warm-up, smoke tests, invite send (cohort A), announce monitoring cadence.
- Hour 0–6: Triage team standing by (see roster below).
- Hour 6–24: Focus on quality signal and high-severity issues.
- Day 1–3: Weekly-ish (daily) KPI sync; decide whether to advance cohort.

Key early KPIs (first 72 hours) — tracker snapshot: (baseline / immediate target)
- Activation rate (accepted invites / invites sent): "10% baseline" / ">=12% target"
- Error rate (5xx + client-timeout per 1k requests): "1.6% baseline" / "<=1% target"
- Median latency (p50 response ms): "240ms baseline" / "<220ms target"
- Quality regression (human eval fail rate on sample prompt set): "6% baseline" / "<=4% target"
- Cost per 1k tokens (inference run rate): "$0.32 baseline" / "<=$0.28 target"
- Support tickets per 100 users (first 72h): "3.2 baseline" / "<=4 acceptable"

Note: these KPIs are intended to be short-lived gating metrics for the beta window (not long-term product KPIs).

Operational roster (first 72h) — owners and contact points:
- Product-Ops lead (on call): Aisha Patel — first responder, coordination, decision owner.
- PM: Marco Lin — customer context, bugs prioritization.
- EM / Serving runtime: Priya Desai — infra triage, rollback authority.
- SRE on-call: Ethan Brooks — incident handling, logs & traces.
- Solutions eng / customer support: rotation team (see linked sheet).
- Escalation to VP Product: Karen Liu (email/sms) if go/no-go required.

First-response checklist (immediate steps for incoming signals):
1) Accept signal (channel = #prodops-beta-A) and create shorthand thread: "beta-A-<short-id>".
2) Triage: severity tagging (sev0, sev1, sev2) using the quick rubric below.
3) Assign owner within 15 minutes.
4) Capture minimal reproducible steps and attach logs/traces link.
5) If sev0/sev1, invoke 30m RTC (real-time call) and pause invite sends for next cohort.
6) For quality regressions (non-infra), run sampling harness and file one-line eval with failing examples.
7) Inform customers in cohort of known impact (templates below) within 60 minutes for sev0 and 3 hours for sev1.

Quick severity rubric (beta window):
- Sev0: Platform unavailable or data loss. Stop rollout, full incident.
- Sev1: Critical degradation (major spikes in 5xx or latency causing user-facing failure). Consider rollback.
- Sev2: Noticeable quality regression affecting >10% of sampled outputs or non-urgent errors. Track and patch.

Communication cadence and templates:
- Slack channel: #beta-window-A (create private channel with all owners).
- Hourly stand-sync for first 6 hours (15 min).
- Twice daily check-ins Days 1–3 (09:30, 16:00 PT).
- Customer template (short): "We’re investigating increased errors affecting X. We’ll follow up in 60m with an update. — Product Team"
- Customer template (update): "Update: root cause identified (infra/quality). Working on fix; ETA ~X. If you need to opt out of the beta now, reply and we’ll remove you."

Dashboards and queries to monitor (links should be populated pre-launch):
- Traffic & health dashboard (p50/p90/p99 latency, 5xx rate, qps) — primary monitor.
- Cost burn dashboard (tokens/CPU-hours per minute).
- Quality eval dashboard (sampled prompts, human-eval pass rate + diff from baseline).
- Error drilldown (top stack traces, model variant, region).
- Live request sampler (store 100 recent requests with masks for PII).

Gating decisions (advancement to next cohort):
Advance if after 48 hours:
- 5xx <= target threshold and trending down OR incidents fully mitigated.
- Quality regression has patch or clear rollback plan.
- No open sev0s and <=1 active sev1 that’s expected to resolve within 24h.
- Stakeholder signoff on readiness checklist (PM, EM, SRE, Product-Ops).

Rollback & fallback patterns (fast options):
- Feature flag off (fastest, ~2–5 min propagation).
- Route to older model variant (compatibility tested) — requires routing team signoff.
- Throttle traffic to beta cohort (set qps cap).
- Pause invite sends (manual).

Contingency runbook snippet (for Sev1+):
1) Triage channel -> gather triage notes.
2) SRE snapshot — collect logs, live trace, node health.
3) If infra: run rollback to v-prev or scale up GPU pool (pre-authorized buckets).
4) If model/quality: switch routing to fallback model variant and enable prefix-cache bypass.
5) Communicate externally (customer update) and internally (incident postmortem owner).

Measurement queries (examples to paste into dashboards):
- Error rate over last 60m: sum(5xx)/sum(requests) by minute.
- Latency quantiles: p50/p90/p99 over rolling 5m window.
- Eval regression delta: compare last 100 sampled evals to baseline set.

Open questions / unknowns (needs follow-up):
- Should we automatically cap cohort invites if cost-per-token is > 20% above prediction? (action: finance + infra to advise).
- Confirm SLA language for beta invites — legal signoff needed on support commitments.
- Who has authority to increase burst capacity for Dedicated customers during beta? (action: infra ops).

Next immediate actions (pre-launch checklist):
- [ ] Populate live dashboards with links (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Draft and pre-approve customer templates (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Add rotation schedule for solutions eng (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Smoke test rollback flows (owner: Priya + SRE).
- [ ] Create Confluence incident template and link in Slack channel (owner: Ethan).

Notes to self / working thoughts (informal):
- Keep messaging short; customers in betas prefer transparency + opt-out.
- Early quality flaps often correlate to prompt distribution mismatch—prepare short prompt transforms or guardrails.
- Avoid broad rollbacks when problems are isolated to one model variant; prefer routing fallback.

Document history: created 2024-11-07 by Aisha Patel; in-review with Marco and Priya 2024-12; major edit 2025-01-15 to KPI thresholds after alpha run.
